artists.biography:
"Rhiannon Giddens"   the singer and multi-instrumentalist is best known as the frontwoman of African-American string band the Carolina Chocolate Drops, whose 2010 album Genuine Negro Jig earned them a Grammy Award for Best Traditional Folk Album. Raised in Piedmont, North Carolina, Giddens studied opera at the Oberlin Conservatory before relocating back home, where she became immersed in the rural musical traditions of that region. 
In 2013 Giddens began pushing further into her solo career. Giddens participated in "Another Day, Another Time", a concert inspired by the Coen brothers film Inside Llewyn Davis. Many critics have stated that Giddens had the best performance at what was called "the concert of the year".

perplexity.description:
Tomorrow Is My Turn is Rhiannon Giddens' debut solo studio album, released on February 10, 2015, by Nonesuch Records. Produced by T Bone Burnett, the album showcases Giddens' versatile vocal range and her ability to reinterpret traditional American music. It blends genres such as blues, folk, country, and world music, featuring songs made famous by artists like Nina Simone, Patsy Cline, and Elizabeth Cotten. The title track is an English adaptation of Charles Aznavour's French song "L'Amour, c'est comme un jour," famously covered by Nina Simone.

Musically, the album highlights Giddens' classical vocal training and her skill in revitalizing traditional folk and Americana styles with emotional depth and nuance. Critics praised the album for its powerful vocals and diverse repertoire, with The Daily Telegraph awarding it five stars and PopMatters giving it a nine out of ten, calling it a herald of a major American artist. It was also nominated for Best Folk Album at the 58th Annual Grammy Awards and won Album of the Year at the inaugural International Folk Music Awards, cementing Giddens' status as a significant voice in contemporary folk and roots music.

Tomorrow Is My Turn occupies a pivotal place in Giddens' discography as her first solo effort following her work with the Carolina Chocolate Drops. It established her as a solo artist capable of bridging historical and modern sounds, setting the stage for subsequent albums that continue to explore and expand the boundaries of American roots music.
